title: DST and leap-second aware quota reset orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our quota reset machinery currently treats epoch boundaries as UTC midnight cutovers or fixed rolling windows. Customers in non-UTC timezones and regions that observe DST (daylight saving time) or are impacted by leap seconds have reported transient over-usage, unexpected partial-day resets, and billing edge-cases when their local midnight crosses an existing rolling window. This ticket proposes an orchestration layer and migration strategy to make quota resets resilient to DST shifts, leap seconds, and tenant-local timezone anchoring for both hosted and reserved capacity customers. Goals: (1) Define a deterministic rule set for timezone-aware resets and tie-breakers around DST transitions and leap seconds; (2) Implement a coordination protocol between the quota allocator, meter, and reserved-pool allocator to avoid double-counting or gaps during a one-second/one-hour boundary; (3) Provide a migration/backfill path and telemetry to reconcile historical discrepancies for customers on legacy windows.
acceptance_criteria: Quota reset service computes tenant-local reset instants deterministically for all supported timezones, including DST transitions and leap-second days
No duplicate quota consumption or gaps observed during DST forward/back transitions in synthetic tests and canary deployment
Reserved capacity windows and hosted rolling epoch align without double-billing when a DST change occurs in a tenant region
Backfill/reconciliation job produces an audit report and corrective adjustments for affected tenants with manual approval flow
End-to-end e2e tests added to CI simulating DST forward/back and a synthetic leap-second insertion
Deployment can be rolled forward/back with feature flag and provides metrics for discrepancy delta per-tenant
tasks: Design: write detailed spec for timezone anchor semantics and tie-breakers for DST and leap-second days (owner: Connor)
Schema: add 'timezone_anchor' (IANA tz) and 'epoch_origin' fields to quota metadata (migration-safe)
Coordinator: implement soft-orchestration in quota-coordinator to defer resets +/- 60s during leap-second windows and +/- 1h during ambiguous DST overlaps
Metering: update metering pipeline to tag usage with tenant-local-reset-id to avoid cross-boundary attribution
Reserved pools: ensure reserved capacity lease renewals consult tenant reset instant to prevent split windows
Backfill: implement reconciliation job that computes expected vs recorded resets and emits corrective ledger entries (dry-run mode first)
Testing: add unit + integration tests for DST forward/back transitions and a leap-second simulator
Telemetry: dashboard showing 'reset offset' incidents, per-tenant discrepancy, and backfill corrections
Docs: update billing FAQ and support playbook with examples and migration notes
Canary: run a canary with 5% of tenants for 48 hours behind feature flag before cluster-wide rollout
comments: 2026-03-04 - Aisha Patel: Kicked off discovery. Pulled examples from 3 customer incident reports where monthly resets shifted by an hour after DST changes. Linked artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.ai/quota/dst-issues and GH issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/7122

2026-03-05 - Connor Miles: Prototype algorithm: store timezone_anchor (IANA) and compute next_reset as 'local midnight in anchor timezone expressed in UTC'. For ambiguous local times (DST fall back) prefer the earlier UTC instant to keep resets monotonic. For skipped local times (DST spring forward) align to the next valid local midnight plus a deterministic offset. Will write spec for tie-breakers.

2026-03-06 - Mei Chen (SRE): Concern: leap-seconds are not handled by standard libraries cleanly. We should treat leap-second days as 'fuzzy' windows and introduce a 120s grace window around 23:59:59 UTC when reconciliation runs. Proposed metric: 'reset_stability' counts resets that deviated by >30s from expected.

2026-03-08 - Billing review (Samir Gupta): Approve approach if backfill ledger entries are strictly additive and do not change previously invoiced totals without manual review. Need audit trail and approval workflow for any retroactive charge adjustments.

2026-03-10 - Design review (Lena Ortiz): UX note - Console should show tenant's timezone anchor and next reset instant in local time. Also add a control to let enterprise customers opt out of timezone anchoring and stay on UTC resets for compliance reasons.

2026-03-11 - Connor Miles: Implementation started. Branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7351 (early coordinator changes). Added feature flag 'quota.tz_anchor_v2' and 'quota.leap_grace_seconds' (default 120).

2026-03-12 - QA (Diego Rivera): Added test harness that replays 90 days of synthetic usage across DST transitions for multiple timezones. Found an edge-case where reserved-pool lease expiry aligned to tenant midnight produces a brief momentary double-counting; adding coordinator fencing to avoid two concurrent active epochs.
